Inverse Probability Weights From User-Supplied Probabilities

Source: R/ipwprob.R
ipwprob.Rd

Computes inverse probability weights from probabilities (or densities) of the observed exposure that you estimated yourself, for example with a machine-learning model or SuperLearner. Point treatment weights are num / den; with id and timevar, the ratios are multiplied cumulatively over time within each subject, as in ipwtm.

Usage

ipwprob(den, num = NULL, id = NULL, timevar = NULL, trunc = NULL)

Arguments

den

Numeric vector: for each row, the probability (or density) of the observed exposure given the covariates of the denominator model.

num

Optional numeric vector of the same length: the probability (or density) of the observed exposure given the covariates of the numerator model. If NULL, unstabilized weights (numerator = 1) are computed.

id

Optional vector of subject identifiers, same length as den. When given, weights are cumulated over time within each subject.

timevar

Numeric vector of follow-up times, same length as den; required when id is given. It sets the order in which the ratios are multiplied within a subject.

trunc

Optional truncation percentile between 0 and 0.5 (e.g., 0.01 for 1st/99th percentiles).

Value

A list of class "ipwprob" containing:

ipw.weights

Numeric vector of inverse probability weights, in the order of the input.

weights.trunc

Numeric vector of truncated weights (if trunc is specified).

call

The original function call.

Details

For time-varying weights of type = "first" or "cens" (see ipwtm), set the probabilities to 1 for the rows after the first switch, so that those rows do not change the cumulative weight.

See also

ipwpoint, ipwtm.

Author

Hung Thai Tran hungtt@oucru.org

Examples

# Point treatment: probabilities from any model, here a logistic regression
set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(l = rnorm(200))
d$a <- rbinom(200, 1, plogis(d$l))
p <- fitted(glm(a ~ l, family = binomial, data = d))
w <- ipwprob(den = ifelse(d$a == 1, p, 1 - p),
             num = ifelse(d$a == 1, mean(d$a), 1 - mean(d$a)))
summary(w$ipw.weights)
#>    Min. 1st Qu.  Median    Mean 3rd Qu.    Max. 
#>  0.5892  0.7849  0.9089  0.9981  1.1440  2.6291 

# Time-varying: the ratios are multiplied within each subject over time
long <- data.frame(id = rep(1:3, each = 2), time = rep(1:2, 3),
                   p = c(0.5, 0.8, 0.4, 0.9, 0.6, 0.7))
ipwprob(den = long$p, id = long$id, timevar = long$time)$ipw.weights
#> [1] 2.000000 2.500000 2.500000 2.777778 1.666667 2.380952
